title: The promise and the fear
about: Ramchal's own illustration of `רמיא` and of `ישוב`, Heb p183, Eng p184. Both labels are his. The two verses enter as `tradition`, so they hold authority before the sugya begins.

units.speaker: Genesis 28:15
units.he: והנה אנכי עמך ושמרתיך בכל אשר־תלך
units.en: Behold I am with you and will protect you wherever you go.

anatomy.note: `בכל אשר תלך`: protection everywhere, the whole class of places.

units.speaker: Genesis 32:8
units.en: And Yaakov was very much afraid.

units.speaker: R. Yaakov bar Idi
units.he: רבי יעקב בר אידי רמי, כתיב … וכתיב
units.en: He raised a contradiction: it is written thus, and it is also written thus.

anatomy.note: Protected everywhere against very much afraid: as posed, a head-on clash.

units.speaker: R. Yaakov bar Idi
units.en: He said: Yaakov thought that perhaps sin may have some bearing on the promise.

anatomy.note: The promise holds in the respect of merit; the fear is about sin having intervened. Not the same respect, so no clash.
`שמא`: said as possible, not as certain.

units.note: A `ישוב`: the one who offers it believes it is true, so it fully discharges the difficulty.
